cf.title: Fix plpgsql's R/W optimization for simple expressions run via SPI

input.subject: [PATCH] Fix plpgsql's R/W optimization for simple expressions run via SPI

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. Message #1 states the bug, gives a reproducer that returns a wrong result on 18 and master, and explains the cause. The fix narrows the read/write optimization to simple expressions and adds no user-visible surface. Confidence is low because only one message is visible and the code was not read.

brief.title: Fix plpgsql read/write expanded-value optimization when simple expression runs via SPI
brief.problem: Since 18, a PL/pgSQL assignment can give a wrong result in builds without assertions, and trips an assertion in builds with them. It happens when the simple expression is busy, so PL/pgSQL runs it through SPI, and SPI has replanned it. The new plan's Params get the read/write "transfer" treatment chosen for a different Param.
brief.proposed_design: plpgsql_param_compile() installs the plpgsql_param_eval_var_check() callback only while compiling the simple expression's own tree. Expressions run through SPI (exec_run_select) get read-only references, as non-simple expressions always do. The patch adds regression tests to plpgsql_array.sql.
author_claims: Master and 18 without assertions return a wrong result for the attached script; 17 and patched master return the correct one.
Assertion-enabled builds of master, 19 and 18 fail Assert("param == expr->expr_rw_param") or Assert(context.count > 0).
The bug needs neither force_generic_plan nor recursion; default plan caching or an error caught in an exception block also triggers it.
The cost is one copy of the value at SPI levels only, in a path that flattens its result anyway.
check-world passes without TAP tests, PL/pgSQL tests pass under Valgrind, and the patch cherry-picks cleanly to 19 and 18.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. Nobody has replied, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review, targeting back-patch to 18.
unclear: The author gives no measurement of the extra copy cost for workloads that often fall back to the SPI path, such as after a caught error.
The author does not say whether he checked other users of expr_rwopt and expr_rw_param on the SPI path, such as the "inplace" method.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author asks for a back-patch to 18 and 19, and the CommitFest entry targets stable branches.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch changes when pl_exec.c installs plpgsql_param_eval_var_check(), a rule that future changes to the read/write optimization must keep.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Simple expressions run through SPI now copy the variable's value, where 18 could transfer it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the "inplace" method, or any other user of expr_rwopt and expr_rw_param, have the same exposure when the expression runs through SPI after a replan?
How much slower is an assignment to a large array when the expression stays busy for the rest of a transaction after a caught error?
Do the TAP tests pass on master, 19 and 18 with the patch applied?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows PL/pgSQL expression execution in pl_exec.c, the expanded-object read/write rules, and how SPI replans cached plans.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the correctness of the read/write optimization on 18, 19 and master for the life of those branches, including any slowdown on the SPI path in a minor release.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has one message, with a reproducer, regression tests and a check on the cherry-pick to 19 and 18.

priority.reason: The patch fixes a wrong result in released 18 that needs a busy simple expression and a replan, so few users hit it, but the result is silently wrong. The patch is 6.4 KB in one source file plus tests, and nobody has replied in the visible thread.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the review could not check that the callback is installed only for the simple expression's own tree, or that the "inplace" method is safe on the SPI path. The memory-safety side of the second reference was also not checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Rearrange execution of PARAM_EXTERN Params for plpgsql's benefit.
Reverted commit(s): Further reduce overhead for passing plpgsql variables to the executor.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This patch does three interrelated things:

* Create a new expression execution step type EEOP_PARAM_CALLBACK
and add the infrastructure needed for add-on modules to generate that.
As discussed, the best control mechanism for that seems to be to add
another hook function to ParamListInfo, which will be called by
ExecInitExpr if it's supplied and a PARAM_EXTERN Param is found.
For stand-alone expressions, we add a new entry point to allow the
ParamListInfo to be specified directly, since it can't be retrieved
from the parent plan node's EState.

* Redesign the API for the ParamListInfo paramFetch hook so that the
ParamExternData array can be entirely virtual.  This also lets us get rid
of ParamListInfo.paramMask, instead leaving it to the paramFetch hook to
decide which param IDs should be accessible or not.  plpgsql_param_fetch
was already doing the identical masking check, so having callers do it too
seemed redundant.  While I was at it, I added a "speculative" flag to
paramFetch that the planner can specify as TRUE to avoid unwanted failures.
This solves an ancient problem for plpgsql that it couldn't provide values
of non-DTYPE_VAR variables to the planner for fear of triggering premature
"record not assigned yet" or "field not found" errors during planning.

* Rework plpgsql to get rid of the need for "unshared" parameter lists,
by dint of turning the single ParamListInfo per estate into a nearly
read-only data structure that doesn't instantiate any per-variable data.
Instead, the paramFetch hook controls access to per-variable data and can
make the right decisions on the fly, replacing the cases that we used to
need multiple ParamListInfos for.  This might perhaps have been a
performance loss on its own, but by using a paramCompile hook we can
bypass plpgsql_param_fetch entirely during normal query execution.
(It's now only called when, eg, we copy the ParamListInfo into a cursor
portal.  copyParamList() or SerializeParamList() effectively instantiate
the virtual parameter array as a simple physical array without a
paramFetch hook, which is what we want in those cases.)  This allows
reverting most of commit 6c82d8d1f, though I kept the cosmetic
code-consolidation aspects of that (eg the assign_simple_var function).

Performance testing shows this to be at worst a break-even change,
and it can provide wins ranging up to 20% in test cases involving
accesses to fields of "record" variables.  The fact that values of
such variables can now be exposed to the planner might produce wins
in some situations, too, but I've not pursued that angle.

In passing, remove the "parent" pointer from the arguments to
ExecInitExprRec and related functions, instead storing that pointer in a
transient field in ExprState.  The ParamListInfo pointer for a stand-alone
expression is handled the same way; we'd otherwise have had to add
yet another recursively-passed-down argument in expression compilation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert inappropriate weakening of an Assert in plpgsql.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert inappropriate weakening of an Assert in plpgsql.
Reverted commit(s): Allow parallel query for prepared statements with generic plans.; Repair bogus handling of multi-assignment Params in upper plan levels.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 682ce911f modified exec_save_simple_expr to accept a Param
in the tlist of a Gather node, rather than the normal case of a Var
referencing the Gather's input.  It turns out that this was a kluge
to work around the bug later fixed in 0f7ec8d9c, namely that setrefs.c
was failing to replace Params in upper plan nodes with Var references
to the same Params appearing in the child tlists.  With that fixed,
there seems no reason to continue to allow a Param here.  (Moreover,
even if we did expect a Param here, the semantically correct thing
to do would be to take the Param as the expression being sought.
Whatever it may represent, it is *not* a reference to the child.)
Hence, revert that part of 682ce911f.

That all happened a long time ago.  However, since the net effect
here is just to tighten an Assert condition, I'm content to change
it only in master.

precedents_retrieved.title: Expand applicability of aggregate's sortop optimization
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the planner keep the index-based MIN/MAX optimization for aggregates with an ORDER BY clause, such as MIN(x ORDER BY x), when the ordering uses the same column and a sort operator from the same btree opfamily as the aggregate's sortop. Later in the thread, Andrei Lepikhov reworked it into an aggregate support function (prosupport) that removes the aggregate's ORDER BY for min/max.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane reviewed the prosupport version and found no documentation for the new support request. He doubted that sharing a btree opfamily justifies removing the ORDER BY clause, given opposite sort directions and plans without an index. He also found no check that the aggregated and ordering expressions match, and questioned whether MIN(x ORDER BY x) occurs often enough to be worth the planning cycles. The original author then closed the entry because the patch had become a different patch, and suggested a new entry for it.
matched_queries: plpgsql expanded array optimization wrong result
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Also, I am far from convinced that the code is right: the fact that the aggsortop shares a btree opfamily with orderClause->sortop doesn't seem to be enough to justify removing the aggorder clause.

precedents_retrieved.title: new plpgsql.extra_errors check - strict_expr_check
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a plpgsql.extra_errors check, strict_expr_check, that allows only a_expr expressions in PL/pgSQL, so undocumented forms such as `var := column FROM tab` are rejected and a missing semicolon before the next statement raises a syntax error. A later version moved the check from the main SQL parser into post-parse checks inside plpgsql, and the check is off by default.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Kirk Wolak marked the patch Ready for Committer in July 2025, and after that the author only posted rebases until the entry was withdrawn. No committer replied in the visible messages.

precedents_retrieved.title: When deleting the plpgsql function, release the CachedPlan of the function
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Matthias van de Meent, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch frees the CachedPlan contexts of a PL/pgSQL function or procedure when DROP FUNCTION or DROP PROCEDURE runs, so they no longer stay in CacheMemoryContext until the session ends. The author showed with pg_get_backend_memory_contexts() that a dropped and recreated procedure leaves two sets of CachedPlan contexts.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch frees cached plans only in the backend that runs the DROP, because other sessions do not execute RemoveFunctionById and keep their plans. Tom Lane suggested that PL/pgSQL, or funccache.c so SQL functions also benefit, install a shared-cache-invalidation callback on pg_proc that marks function trees as deletable. The author agreed, linked a new thread, and withdrew this entry. Vladlen Popolitov also asked why the plans should be freed at all.
matched_queries: plpgsql simple expression replan cached plan
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It doesn't, which is (one reason) why it's just a crude hack.

precedents_retrieved.title: When deleting the plpgsql function, release the CachedPlan of the function
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch frees a plpgsql function's compiled parse tree, and the cached plans it links to through SPI, when the function is dropped or invalidated, so the memory is not leaked. A later version registers a syscache callback in cached_function_compile and adds a hash table that maps invalidation hash values to function keys.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane called dropping the function-cache entry a reasonable idea, and the author reported that the new version still emitted duplicate warnings. The last message is a patch update on 2025-09-05 with no reply before the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: plpgsql - possibility to get element or array type for referenced variable type
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets PL/pgSQL `%TYPE` refer to variables of composite type, including polymorphic parameters. It also adds syntax to derive the array type or the element type of a referenced variable, first as `%ARRAYTYPE`/`%ELEMENTTYPE` and later as `%TYPE[]` and `ELEMENT OF ...%TYPE`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane proposed rejecting this PL/pgSQL-only implementation. He wanted these type operators added to the core grammar's Typename production, so PL/pgSQL would pick them up automatically. Joe Conway and Jim Nasby agreed. The author then found that a reduced patch with only the composite `%TYPE` fix gave too little benefit, and asked for it to be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I played with the reduced patch, and the benefit without all other things
is negligible. It should be rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Expand the use of check_canonical_path() for more GUCs
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch applied check_canonical_path() to more path GUCs: promote_trigger_file, krb_server_keyfile and the ssl_* file settings. It also added comments in guc.c explaining why data_directory, config_file, hba_file and ident_file already get canonicalized at postmaster startup.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned why any GUC needs check_canonical_path(); he found the remaining calls in guc.c were leftovers from when data_directory and config_file were canonicalized there, and noted that canonicalize_path() does not make relative paths absolute. Tom Lane said user-given strings should not be altered without need, and that canonicalization matters only where other paths are derived from the value. The author concluded there was consensus to perhaps remove some canonicalization but not to expand it.

precedents_retrieved.title: use regular expressions to simplify less_greater and not_equals
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the SQL lexer to match both "<>" and "!=" with one regular expression, (<>|!=), under the not_equals definition. It removes the separate less_greater definition, which the author said confuses developers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found the change less clear because it moves the comment on <>-means-!= away from the code that implements it. He added that it would get in the way if <> and != ever needed different treatment. Andrew Dunstan saw no benefit and did not agree the current code confuses developers. David G. Johnston leaned toward keeping the status quo, the author gave no stronger argument, and Tom Lane marked it rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file"
Reverted commit(s): Rename routines for write/read of pgstats file
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit ed823da1289, that has made pgstat_write_chunk() and
pgstat_read_chunk() available for public use.  These routines do not
have a symmetric API definition across reads and writes, with the write
part returning a void status, deferring an error detection once all the
stats entries have been processed with an ferror(), and the read part
returning a boolean status.

These routines are just tiny wrappers around fread() and fwrite(), and
extensions can just define they own routines instead of relying on the
same facilities as the core pgstat.c.  This commit removes their
declaration from the public headers, to reduce the confusion.
test_custom_stats is updated to use its own read/write routines.
Perhaps something better could be designed in the future; trying to do
so for v19 is not feasable during beta.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent matches. [P1] is in the same area, since it added the PARAM_EXTERN callback machinery that plpgsql_param_compile() builds on. Its recorded text describes what that commit does, not a reason for rejection that applies to this bug fix. Message #1 points only to the thread that introduced the "transfer" method, which is the origin of the bug and not an earlier attempt at this fix.

The patch changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog, pg_dump output, psql behaviour or client-visible protocol. The only behaviour change makes 18 and later return the results 17 returned, so there is nothing to object to from the compatibility angle. Back-patching to 18 adds no user-facing contract.

The fix changes only in-memory PL/pgSQL behaviour in pl_exec.c, with regression tests. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalog or wire protocol. The commit message mentions no struct or exported-function change, so back-patching to 18 shows no ABI risk; this is provisional without the code.

The fix narrows when PL/pgSQL hands a read/write expanded value to an expression; it adds no privilege, role, GUC, view or interface. Expressions run through SPI get read-only references, which is the safer default. A memory-safety angle (a second reference reading a freed or moved value) could not be checked without the code; the reported symptom is a null read.

This is a back-patchable bug fix that narrows an 18-era optimization back to the case its own comment allows: simple expressions only. Expressions run through SPI fall back to read-only references, which is how 17 handled them and how non-simple expressions are handled now. The extra copy lands only on the SPI path, which flattens its result anyway. The patch adds no new API, GUC or catalog state, and puts no cost on users who never take that path. [P1] concerns a different, larger redesign of Param execution and does not apply. Without the code, two points remain unchecked: whether the "inplace" method has the same SPI-path exposure, and whether long transactions that follow a caught error copy large arrays often.

This is a bug fix for a wrong result in the 18 transfer optimization, inside pl_exec.c. No existing feature, extension or setting covers it, and it adds no new mechanism. Turning the optimization off would mean reverting it, which is the larger change. Only the code can show whether the fix is correct.

This is a wrong-result bug fix in released 18, with a reproducer in message #1 that works under default plan caching, so demand is not in question. The cost is one extra copy on the SPI fallback path only, and it falls on the affected expressions. Precedent [P1] concerns the PARAM_EXTERN callback design and does not bear on demand.
